question.problem:
Which of the following matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since ${a}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition  II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since ${b}_{21}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $C$ is in row echelon form.
